item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J02750","case1_error":"Omits Saturday’s ten additional rounds, counting only one Saturday round.","case2_error":"Divides the international surcharge by all four letters instead of the two international letters.","reason":"One omits a stated contribution; the other allocates a surcharge over the wrong group.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02751","case1_error":"Labels 45 training days as weeks without dividing by five training days per week.","case2_error":"Leading answer marker says 25, but the derivation and concluding answer correctly give 15 seconds.","reason":"Case 2 has only an answer-marker conflict, so a shared mathematical error cannot be established.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J02752","case1_error":"Falsely equates current practice P with past practice P/2, then asserts P=2P and x=2.","case2_error":"Incorrectly evaluates the written expression as 76−46=30; also describes savings remaining rather than spending, though these are equal here.","reason":"Case 1 introduces false relations; case 2 numerically miscalculates an expression that yields the requested amount because half remains.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02753","case1_error":"Counts Reece’s ladder only once, omitting his 15 climbs.","case2_error":"Gives unsupported 40.0 after a correct percentage formula; the correct percentage is 20%.","reason":"Case 1 omits a repetition factor; case 2 supplies an incorrect final number without showing its calculation.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02754","case1_error":"Supplies unsupported 12000 after correctly writing 3000+(276×48)+7000, which equals 23248.","case2_error":"Supplies unsupported 4600 after correctly writing (60×8×14)+2500, which equals 9220.","reason":"Both provide incorrect final numbers after correct formulas, with no intermediate evaluation identifying a more specific arithmetic mistake.","judgment":"same"}]}
